params.question: CAUTI, CLABSI, and VAP are grouped together in HAI classification because they share which key feature?

answers.text: They are all caused exclusively by Gram-negative organisms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Not quite. While many HAI organisms are Gram-negative, CLABSI is commonly caused by Gram-positive coagulase-negative staphylococci and MRSA. The shared feature is their association with indwelling devices, not a common organism profile.

answers.text: They are all associated with indwelling medical devices

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. CAUTI involves urinary catheters, CLABSI involves central venous catheters, and VAP involves endotracheal tubes. This device association makes them targetable through bundled care — standardised insertion and maintenance practices.

answers.text: They all develop within 24 hours of hospital admission

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. CAUTI requires at least 2 days of catheterisation, and VAP develops 48 hours or more after intubation. The timing varies, but the unifying feature is their link to indwelling devices.

answers.text: They all respond to the same empirical antibiotic regimen

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Each HAI type involves different organisms with different resistance profiles — E. coli and Klebsiella in CAUTI differ significantly from Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter in VAP.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key feature is device association. CAUTI, CLABSI, and VAP each involve an indwelling device (catheter, central line, endotracheal tube), which is why bundled prevention care targeting device insertion and maintenance is so effective.

Well done! Recognising device association is clinically important because it means prevention bundles — standardised insertion, daily review of device necessity, and timely removal — can significantly reduce all three infections.

params.question: In the chain of transmission of healthcare-associated infections, which link is the primary target of most infection control interventions?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While identifying the causative organism is essential for treatment, we cannot eliminate all pathogens from the hospital environment. Most interventions focus on how organisms move between patients.
Host factors such as immunosuppression and extremes of age increase risk, but these are often not modifiable. The largest number of interventions target an earlier, more actionable link.

Correct. Contact transmission via healthcare workers' hands is the most common route. Hand hygiene alone prevents more HAIs than any other single intervention, making this the most actionable link in the chain.

Reducing portals of entry — for example, removing catheters early — does help, but the mode of transmission is targeted by the greatest number of interventions, from hand hygiene to barrier precautions to surface disinfection.

overallFeedback.feedback: The mode of transmission is the primary target. Contact transmission — especially via healthcare workers' hands — accounts for the majority of HAI spread, and hand hygiene is the single most effective intervention.

Exactly right. Contact transmission is the dominant mode, and hand hygiene is the single most effective intervention in preventing HAIs — this is why infection control programmes focus heavily on this link.

interactions.label: NDM-1 (New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase) resistance has spread rapidly across di

params.question: NDM-1 (New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase) resistance has spread rapidly across different bacterial species, primarily through which mechanism?

answers.text: Intrinsic impermeability encoded in the bacterial chromosome

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Intrinsic resistance is a fixed, species-specific trait — for example, Pseudomonas's naturally impermeable outer membrane. NDM-1 is acquired resistance that transfers between entirely different species, requiring a mobile genetic mechanism.

answers.text: Spontaneous chromosomal point mutations under antibiotic selective pressure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chromosomal mutations can produce resistance, but they are slow and remain within one lineage. NDM-1 crosses species boundaries rapidly because it is carried on transferable genetic elements, not on the chromosome.

answers.text: Clonal spread of a single resistant strain from patient to patient

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Clonal spread transmits the same resistant strain between patients, typically on hands. NDM-1, however, moves between entirely different bacterial species — Klebsiella to E. coli, for instance — which requires horizontal gene transfer.

Correct. NDM-1 is encoded on plasmids — self-replicating mobile genetic elements that transfer between unrelated bacterial species during conjugation. This is why NDM-1 disseminated globally so rapidly after its identification in New Delhi.

overallFeedback.feedback: NDM-1 spreads via plasmids — mobile DNA elements that hop between different bacterial species through horizontal gene transfer. This is fundamentally different from clonal spread or chromosomal mutations and explains its rapid global dissemination.

Well done. Plasmid-mediated horizontal gene transfer is the key reason NDM-1 poses such a serious threat — it can jump between species, making containment far harder than for clonally spreading resistance.

interactions.label: A patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis requires which category of transmis

params.question: A patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis requires which category of transmission-based precautions beyond standard precautions?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Contact precautions are for organisms spread by direct or indirect touch, such as MRSA and C. difficile. Tuberculosis spreads through the air as tiny droplet nuclei, requiring a higher level of respiratory protection.

answers.text: Droplet precautions with a surgical mask and one-metre separation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Droplet precautions protect against larger respiratory particles (>5 μm) from organisms like influenza. TB spreads via droplet nuclei (<5 μm) that remain suspended in air for hours — a surgical mask cannot filter these effectively.

answers.text: Airborne precautions with an N95 respirator and negative-pressure room

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Mycobacterium tuberculosis spreads via droplet nuclei that remain airborne and can travel long distances. Negative pressure prevents contaminated air from escaping, and an N95 respirator filters particles down to 0.3 μm.
Protective isolation shields immunocompromised patients from environmental organisms. TB isolation does the opposite — it protects others from the patient's infectious respiratory secretions.

overallFeedback.feedback: Tuberculosis requires airborne precautions — a negative-pressure room, an N95 respirator, and a closed door — because its droplet nuclei are small enough to remain suspended in air and travel long distances.
Correct. TB, measles, and varicella are the classic airborne-precaution organisms because their droplet nuclei can float and linger in air, requiring negative pressure and N95-level filtration.

interactions.label: During doffing (removal) of PPE after caring for a patient on contact precaution

params.question: During doffing (removal) of PPE after caring for a patient on contact precautions, which item should be removed first to minimise the risk of self-contamination?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Gloves are the most heavily contaminated item and are removed first using the glove-into-glove technique. Hand hygiene follows immediately, before touching any other equipment. The full doffing order is: gloves → hand hygiene → eye protection → gown → mask → hand hygiene.
The gown is removed after eye protection, not first. Removing it while wearing contaminated gloves would transfer organisms from the glove surface to your scrubs and skin.
Eye protection is removed after gloves and hand hygiene, using only the ear pieces. The correct doffing order is: gloves → hand hygiene → eye protection → gown → mask → hand hygiene.
The mask or respirator is removed last during doffing. Removing it first would expose your face to contamination while handling other contaminated PPE items.

overallFeedback.feedback: Gloves are removed first because they are the most contaminated item. The full doffing sequence is: gloves → hand hygiene → eye protection → gown → mask → hand hygiene. Every step protects you from the contaminated surfaces being removed.
Well done. The doffing sequence is designed so that each step avoids transferring contamination — gloves off first (most contaminated), mask off last (protects your airway throughout the process).

interactions.label: The acceptable standard for Escherichia coli in hospital drinking water is fewer

params.question: The acceptable standard for Escherichia coli in hospital drinking water is fewer than 10 colony-forming units per 100 millilitres.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The standard is stricter than you might expect — it requires ZERO E. coli per 100 mL. Because E. coli is a faecal indicator organism, even a single colony signals contamination and makes the water unacceptable for consumption.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Well done. The standard is ZERO E. coli per 100 mL of drinking water. E. coli is a faecal indicator organism — any detectable presence signals contamination from human or animal waste, making the water unsafe regardless of how few organisms are found.
